name: hCG

lead: hCG is a pregnancy hormone that imitates LH. Men on testosterone or anabolic steroids use it to maintain testicular size and function, supporting natural hormone production alongside muscle and beard goals.

It binds the LH receptor, prompting the testes to make testosterone from Leydig cells. Medically it triggers ovulation, treats some male hypogonadism, supports fertility treatment and is used as a tumor marker. Some posters discuss it for facial or bone changes; no studies were found on appearance outcomes.

paras: It is a prescription product used in medicine and, in forums, added to testosterone protocols during and after cycles. It is made from the urine of pregnant women or by recombinant DNA.

Reference warnings include thromboembolism and multiple pregnancy in women, and precocious puberty risk in prepubescent boys. It is prescription-only in the US and banned in several sports. The FDA has stated over-the-counter hCG weight-loss products are fraudulent.

angle.text: hCG mimics LH so the testes keep producing testosterone, helping maintain hormone levels and physique during testosterone use. Its role is established in medicine; effects on looks have not been studied.

lead: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is a hormone made by the placenta that resembles luteinizing hormone (LH) and can trigger ovulation in women and stimulate testosterone production in the testes [1]. Pharmaceutical hCG is prescription-only and is made from the urine of pregnant women or by recombinant DNA [1].

In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities hCG is discussed mainly by men using testosterone or anabolic steroids, who say it helps maintain testicular size and function during and after cycles [2][3]. Some posters also discuss it alongside other compounds for facial or bone changes, claims for which no studies were found.

In medicine hCG treats some forms of male hypogonadism, supports fertility treatment, and is used as a tumor marker [1][4]. The FDA has stated over-the-counter hCG weight-loss products are fraudulent [1].

paras: In fertility treatment, ovulation occurs about 38 to 40 hours after a single hCG injection, and IVF patients typically receive it to trigger ovulation [1]. In men, hCG stimulates Leydig cells to produce testosterone, treats some hypogonadism, and can preserve fertility and prevent testicular atrophy during testosterone replacement [1][4]. It does not work when the testes cannot make testosterone [4]. The beta subunit is secreted by cancers such as seminoma and choriocarcinoma, so it serves as a tumor marker [1].

Forum users on looksmax.org say hCG is started alongside testosterone to prevent testicular atrophy as signaling from the pituitary declines [3], and some describe it as optional for lower-dose regimens [2]. Anabolic steroids suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, and reference sources confirm users take hCG during and after cycles to mimic LH [1].
hCG is a glycoprotein of 237 amino acids with an alpha subunit shared with LH, FSH and TSH and a unique beta subunit [1]. A carboxy-terminal peptide gives it a longer half-life than LH [1].

Reference warnings for women include ectopic pregnancy, multiple pregnancy, pregnancy loss and thromboembolism; in men prolonged use can increase androgen production, and caution applies in prepubescent teenagers because of the risk of precocious puberty or premature epiphyseal closure [1].

Albert Simeons proposed low-dose hCG with a very-low-calorie diet for weight loss; in 1976 the FDA required a disclaimer, a 1995 meta-analysis concluded no scientific evidence supports effectiveness, and the AMA adopted a policy in 2016 that weight-loss use is inappropriate [1]. In December 2011 the FDA and FTC moved against unapproved hCG products [1].
hCG is on some sports' banned-substance lists, and athletes in MLB, the NFL and UFC have been sanctioned [1].

Registered trials include recombinant hCG for follicle maturation in IVF (NCT01081756, n=218), urinary versus recombinant hCG on oocyte maturity (NCT01507376, n=180) and hormonal stimulation of spermatogenesis in men with azoospermia (NCT05483621, n=100) [5][6][7]. No studies were found of hCG for facial appearance outcomes.
